data.narrative:
The Lumber Manufactory is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Michael Grasso and Andrew Arsht that has raised $53.1M to date. Valuation analysis triangulates across a peer set of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including Series B and D-stage firms such as Exotec ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), Dexterity ($1.6B), Hadrian ($1.6B), and others.

Two methods anchor the valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C progression to the $53.1M total raised, implying $90M. Peer-median analysis across seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in stage advancement and capital efficiency within the peer cohort.

Triangulation produces a low case of $77M, median of $870M, and high case of $1.9B. The stage-progression method yields substantially lower results than peer-median, suggesting either that The Lumber Manufactory commands a discount to public-market robotics valuations or that peer multiples reflect sector momentum not yet reflected in traditional step-up frameworks. Key uncertainties include revenue run-rate, gross margin profile, and relative competitive position versus the named peer set.
